The value is Tier 3 (a filesystem path resolved against live on-disk state, the local auth.db that `LocalAuthProvider._get_conn` opens on every connection). The handler is not a swallow: its whole body is the second arm of an open-or-create protocol -- `descriptor = os.open(path, flags | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600); created = True` -- so a missing file is CREATED exclusively and the function continues with a bound `descriptor`; any failure of that create other than `FileExistsError` propagates unchanged, and the sibling `except OSError as exc:` arm converts `ELOOP` into `LocalAuthStorageSecurityError` and re-raises everything else. Nothing is defaulted and no auth outcome is derived from the miss: a missing database is a first boot, not an authentication result. R6 misfires because `_handler_is_silent` sees neither `raise` nor `return`; the explicit outcome is the bound `descriptor`. R6 `except FileExistsError:` on the exclusive create inside the `FileNotFoundError` arm of `_open_owner_only_database`. Tier 3 as above. This is the lost-race arm of open-or-create: between the failed plain open and `os.open(path, flags | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)` another process created the path, so the handler reopens it with the ORIGINAL no-follow flags -- `descriptor = os.open(path, flags)` -- and leaves `created = False`. It is not a swallow: `descriptor` is bound from the reopen, any failure of that reopen propagates (the enclosing `except OSError as exc:` is a sibling of the outer try, not of this handler, so only ELOOP is translated and every other error is re-raised), and the file the race winner created is subjected to exactly the same control as any pre-existing file: `os.fstat(descriptor)` must be a regular file owned by the current euid with `st_nlink == 1` and mode `0o600`, else `LocalAuthStorageSecurityError` and `os.close`. That check is what stops a racing writer from substituting a wider-mode or hard-linked file for our database, and it runs whether or not this arm executed. No authentication outcome is derived here; the function only admits or refuses a descriptor. R6 misfires because the explicit outcome is a bound name rather than a raise/return.
